title: VPC risk scenario linearizer and tenant mitigation strip
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Problem: Operators managing Private/VPC deployments need a compact, actionable surface inside the Redwood Console that linearizes potential network and capacity failure scenarios and maps them to tenant-facing mitigations and cost exposure. Existing status pages are good for signals but not for scenario exploration or quick mitigations during a rollout. Goal: Design a "mitigation strip" UI that sits on cluster and tenant pages showing prioritized risk scenarios, expected customer impact, recommended playbook actions (one-click where possible), and a cost-surge preview. The strip needs to be dense, scannable, and suitable for both on-call operators and product engineers running canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Design artifacts include a hi-fi prototype of the mitigation strip in both cluster and tenant contexts (desktop) with responsive rules for narrow consoles.
Strip shows 3 prioritized scenarios per tenant with: title, severity, short impact sentence, estimated cost delta (tokens/min or $/hr), and an explicit recommended action button.
Prototype includes a lightweight timeline view showing immediate (0-30m), short (30m-3h), and medium (3h-24h) cost exposure estimates and links to the rollout manager.
Interaction patterns for one-click mitigations are specified (disabled state, confirm modal, audit copy for console logs) and reviewed by Security/Compliance.
Usability test with at least 6 operators demonstrates faster time-to-decision compared to current status page (target median improvement >= 25%).
Design handoff packaged with component tokens, spacing, color semantics for severity (accessible contrast), and copy guidelines for fallback scenarios.
decisions: Surface limited to three prioritized scenarios to keep cognitive load low; allow expansion to full list via chevron.
Estimated cost exposure displayed as a single-line summary with tooltip for token and $ breakdowns; avoids heavy numeric tables on first glance.
One-click actions will call existing infra playbook endpoints; a confirm modal with audit text is required for destructive mitigations.
Mitigation strip will be a reusable component across cluster, tenant, and rollout pages to reduce design/engineering overhead.
tradeoffs: Showing cost exposure at a glance simplifies decision-making but risks underspecifying edge-case billing complexity — mitigated by deep-dive tooltip and link to cost explorer.
One-click mitigations improve Mean Time To Mitigate (MTTM) but increase blast-radius risk; added guardrails (confirm, permission gating, and automatic rollback) chosen to reduce risk.
Keeping the strip compact reduces information density for advanced operators; we provide an expand-to-detailed view for power users.
next_steps: Finalize copy and severity color tokens with accessibility engineer (due 2025-03-04).
Sync with Runtime team to map mitigation actions to infra endpoints and required telemetry fields (API contract draft).
Run 6 participant usability tests with on-call engineers and SREs (sessions scheduled 2025-03-06 to 2025-03-10).
Prepare engineering handoff (components, spacing, interaction states) after design review on 2025-03-12.
components: MitigationStrip (atom): severity badge, headline, impact line, cost-spark, action button, expand chevron
CostMiniTimeline (molecule): three-segment timeline with relative bar and % change
ConfirmModal (component): templated audit copy + confirm checkbox for destructive actions
ExpandableDetail (organism): full scenario diagnostics, logs link, related dashboards
test_plan: Usability: 6 sessions targeting SREs and on-call engineers; metrics: time-to-decision, confidence rating pre/post, error rate when selecting mitigation. Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard navigation checked against WCAG 2.1 AA. Integration: smoke tests with staged infra endpoints to verify action buttons trigger expected playbook responses and generate audit log entries.
